class LockCodeManagerUserSubentryFlow(ConfigSubentryFlow):
    """Add or edit one user of a Lock Code Manager entry."""

    # Whether the add or edit form has a Password field, decided when the
    # dialog first draws it and kept for every re-show. The entry's answer can
    # change while the dialog is open (a reload, a lock still setting up, a
    # lock added elsewhere): a submit read against a fresh answer would
    # delete a stored password the form never showed or overwrite one the
    # user typed, and a re-show after an error that dropped the field would
    # lose one the user typed or bring back one they cleared. None until
    # drawn, so a submit with no form behind it keeps the stored password.
    _password_offered: bool | None = None

    async def async_step_user(
        self, user_input: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    ) -> SubentryFlowResult:
        """Offer to add one user or a block of them."""
        return self.async_show_menu(step_id="user", menu_options=["one", "several"])

    async def async_step_one(
        self, user_input: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    ) -> SubentryFlowResult:
        """Add a user, issuing them a credential position."""
        entry = self._get_entry()
        config = get_entry_config(entry)
        errors: dict[str, str] = {}
        description_placeholders: dict[str, Any] = {}

        if user_input is not None:
            name, fields, errors, placeholders = _validate_user_form(
                self.hass, user_input, config.users
            )
            description_placeholders.update(placeholders)

            if not errors:
                assert name is not None
                # Asked for room for everyone the entry will hold, not for one
                # more: allocation answers about a whole configuration, and a
                # lock too full for the result must refuse before anything is
                # written. Everybody already here keeps their number by tenure
                # and needs no read; only the newcomer's is looked for.
                (
                    unavailable,
                    allocation_errors,
                    allocation_placeholders,
                ) = await _allocate_for(
                    self.hass,
                    entry,
                    config.locks,
                    len(config.users) + 1,
                    held=config.assignment.held_by(config.users),
                )
                if unavailable is None:
                    errors.update(allocation_errors)
                    description_placeholders.update(allocation_placeholders)
                else:
                    # Reconciled against what the entry already holds, so
                    # everybody already here keeps their number and only the
                    # newcomer is issued one.
                    slot = config.assignment.reconcile(
                        {**config.users, name: fields},
                        start=1,
                        unavailable=unavailable,
                    ).slots[identity(name)]
                    warning = _cannot_report(self.hass, config.locks, [slot])
                    return self.async_create_entry(
                        title=name,
                        data={**fields, CONF_SLOT: slot},
                        description="cannot_report" if warning else None,
                        description_placeholders=warning,
                    )

        if self._password_offered is None:
            self._password_offered = _offers_password(entry)
        return self.async_show_form(
            step_id="one",
            data_schema=self.add_suggested_values_to_schema(
                _code_slot_schema(password=REDACTED, user_input or {}
            ),
            errors=errors,
            description_placeholders=description_placeholders,
        )

    async def async_step_several(
        self, user_input: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    ) -> SubentryFlowResult:
        """
        Add a block of users at once, one subentry each.

        The same shape and the same validator the setup flow's yaml path
        uses, so what a person pastes to set the entry up is what they paste
        to add to it. Adding them one at a time is the same work spread over
        one dialog and one lock read each; here it is one read and one write,
        which on a lock that answers an index per round trip is the
        difference between usable and not, and which settles the entry once
        rather than once per arrival.

        This does not touch anybody already here: a block that names one of
        them is refused rather than merged. Editing and removing stay where
        they were, one user at a time, so there is still exactly one way to
        change a user who exists.
        """
        entry = self._get_entry()
        config = get_entry_config(entry)
        errors: dict[str, str] = {}
        description_placeholders: dict[str, Any] = {}

        if user_input:
            (
                users,
                validation_errors,
                validation_placeholders,
            ) = await _async_validate_users_yaml(
                self.hass,
                entry,
                user_input[CONF_USERS],
                config.locks,
                taken=config.users,
            )
            errors.update(validation_errors)
            description_placeholders.update(validation_placeholders)

            if not errors:
                assert users is not None
                # One allocation for the whole block, sized to what the entry
                # will hold once it lands. Everybody already here keeps their
                # number by tenure and is not read for.
                (
                    unavailable,
                    allocation_errors,
                    allocation_placeholders,
                ) = await _allocate_for(
                    self.hass,
                    entry,
                    config.locks,
                    len(config.users) + len(users),
                    held=config.assignment.held_by(config.users),
                )
                if unavailable is None:
                    errors.update(allocation_errors)
                    description_placeholders.update(allocation_placeholders)
                else:
                    arrived = {**config.users, **users}
                    assignment = config.assignment.reconcile(
                        arrived, start=1, unavailable=unavailable
                    )
                    # Written through the one write path rather than by
                    # completing the flow: a finished subentry flow creates
                    # exactly one subentry, and this creates as many as were
                    # pasted.
                    async_write_entry_config(
                        self.hass,
                        entry,
                        EntryConfig(
                            locks=config.locks,
                            users=arrived,
                            assignment=assignment,
                            extra=config.extra,
                        ),
                    )
                    warning = _cannot_report(
                        self.hass,
                        config.locks,
                        (assignment.slots[identity(name)] for name in users),
                    )
                    return self.async_abort(
                        reason="users_added_cannot_report"
                        if warning
                        else "users_added",
                        description_placeholders={
                            "num_users": str(len(users)),
                            **(warning or {}),
                        },
                    )

        return self.async_show_form(
            step_id="several",
            data_schema=_users_schema(user_input),
            errors=errors,
            description_placeholders=description_placeholders,
        )

    async def async_step_reconfigure(
        self, user_input: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    ) -> SubentryFlowResult:
        """Edit a user, who keeps the position they already hold."""
        entry = self._get_entry()
        subentry = self._get_reconfigure_subentry()
        config = get_entry_config(entry)
        errors: dict[str, str] = {}
        description_placeholders: dict[str, Any] = {}
        held = normalize_name(subentry.title)

        # Everybody except the person being edited. Both the name check and,
        # below, the count allocation is asked for are about the OTHERS: the
        # edited user is already in `config.users`, so counting them again
        # refuses on a lock with exactly enough room, and reconciling against
        # a dict that still holds their old name issues their new one a
        # second number.
        others = {other: user for other, user in config.users.items() if other != held}

        if user_input is not None:
            # Not offered by this entry's locks, still the user's (spec
            # decision 10): the form did not show it, so it cannot have
            # cleared it.
            carried = (
                {CONF_PASSWORD: kept}
                if not self._password_offered
                and (kept := subentry.data.get(CONF_PASSWORD))
                else {}
            )
            # Compared with the user as read, PIN stripped: one stored with
            # padding is the same PIN submitted without it.
            name, fields, errors, placeholders = _validate_user_form(
                self.hass,
                user_input,
                others,
                config.users.get(held, subentry.data),
                carried,
            )
            description_placeholders.update(placeholders)

            if not errors:
                assert name is not None
                # The number rides along untouched. It is what every identifier
                # and every lock's credential index is keyed on, so a rename
                # that moved it would rewrite this user's code on every lock
                # and orphan their entities.
                #
                # A subentry with no number at all is not something this
                # integration writes -- hand-edited storage or a half-finished
                # write leaves one. Editing it issues one rather than raising,
                # because a dialog that can only fail leaves the user with no
                # way to repair the record from the UI.
                held_slot = subentry.data.get(CONF_SLOT)
                if held_slot is None:
                    (
                        unavailable,
                        allocation_errors,
                        allocation_placeholders,
                    ) = await _allocate_for(
                        self.hass,
                        entry,
                        config.locks,
                        len(others) + 1,
                        held=config.assignment.held_by(others),
                    )
                    if unavailable is None:
                        errors.update(allocation_errors)
                        description_placeholders.update(allocation_placeholders)
                        return self._async_show_reconfigure(
                            subentry, user_input, errors, description_placeholders
                        )
                    held_slot = config.assignment.reconcile(
                        {**others, name: fields},
                        start=1,
                        unavailable=unavailable,
                    ).slot(name)

                return self.async_update_and_abort(
                    entry,
                    subentry,
                    title=name,
                    data={**fields, CONF_SLOT: held_slot},
                )

        return self._async_show_reconfigure(
            subentry, user_input, errors, description_placeholders
        )

    def _async_show_reconfigure(
        self,
        subentry: ConfigSubentry,
        user_input: dict[str, Any] | None,
        errors: dict[str, str],
        description_placeholders: dict[str, Any],
    ) -> SubentryFlowResult:
        """Render the edit form, prefilled from the submission or the record."""
        if self._password_offered is None:
            self._password_offered = _offers_password(self._get_entry())
        return self.async_show_form(
            step_id="reconfigure",
            # A password the form does not offer has no field, so the
            # suggestions cannot echo it.
            data_schema=self.add_suggested_values_to_schema(
                _code_slot_schema(password=REDACTED,
                user_input
                or {
                    key: value
                    for key, value in subentry.data.items()
                    if key != CONF_SLOT
                }
                | {CONF_NAME: subentry.title},
            ),
            errors=errors,
            description_placeholders=description_placeholders,
        )

content.thinking:
I'm thinking through how the validation function should accept which credential types are being offered, with setup flow restricted to PIN-only while subentry and reconfigure flows pull from the entry's available types once loaded. I also need to account for a latch that tracks whether the password field was shown when the dialog first rendered, since that affects how submissions without that field get handled.

For the actual credential-required rule, I'm weighing whether to use that latched offered-types value or recompute it fresh at submit time -- fresh feels more accurate since it reflects the lock's true state at save time, though it could create inconsistency if the lock's runtime_data becomes unavailable mid-reload between when the form was shown and when it's submitted.

Using the latched value sidesteps that confusing edge case where a password typed into a password-offering form gets rejected as a "missing credential" just because the entry reloaded in between. So I lean toward defining offered types as PIN plus password if the latch says password was offered, falling back to computing it only if the latch is still None at submit. But I need to be careful: changing when the latch gets set to True affects the "carried" logic in reconfigure, since a None latch currently means "carry the stored password if no form was drawn" -- flipping the latch to True at submit would wipe that carried password if the user input lacks one, which breaks the intended behavior.

I'm sketching a helper that returns PIN-only before the entry is loaded, or the full available credential types once runtime data exists, plus a companion function checking whether password is among those offered types. Now I'm weighing whether the subentry form rule should use this fresh computation or the latched value -- the coordinator and service already use the fresh version, treating "offered" as any lock in the entry accepting that type, so consistency might favor fresh over latched here too.

Going with fresh offered types at submit time is semantically correct here — if a lock requiring a password shows up, a carried stored password should count since it's genuinely usable now, which matches the design intent even if it means a password-only submission after reload gets refused and must be retried. I should also update the docstring language to clarify credentials only count toward what an enabled user needs if their type is actually offered.

Now I need to figure out where "offered" types get computed — setup flow with a code_slot only offers PIN, setup YAML only offers PIN, and there's an `_offered_types(entry)` helper. The validation function should derive offered types from the config_entry itself when present, falling back to PIN-only during setup, since it already knows whether it's the setup flow or an entry's step. I also need to check whether the error key should be "invalid_config" from the schema validation or "missing_credential_if_enabled" as used on the YAML path today, so I should check the relevant test cases to confirm.

async def _set_slot1_password(hass: HomeAssistant, entry, value: str) -> None:
    await hass.services.async_call(
        DOMAIN,
        SERVICE_SET_CREDENTIAL,
        {
            CONF_NAME: "slot1",
            ATTR_CREDENTIAL_TYPE: "password",
            ATTR_CREDENTIAL_VALUE: value,
            "config_entry_id": entry.entry_id,
        },
        blocking=True,
    )


async def test_emptying_an_offered_password_in_the_edit_form_removes_it(
    hass: HomeAssistant, lcm_config_entry
) -> None:
    """The form showed the password, so leaving it empty clears it."""
    await _set_slot1_password(hass, lcm_config_entry, "pw")
    result = await _edit_user_form(hass, lcm_config_entry, 1)

    result = await _subentry_configure(
        hass,
        result["flow_id"],
        {CONF_NAME: "slot1", CONF_ENABLED: True, CONF_PIN: "1234"},
    )

    assert result["type"] == "abort"
    assert not get_entry_config(lcm_config_entry).slot(1).get("password")


async def test_emptying_every_credential_of_an_enabled_user_is_refused(
    hass: HomeAssistant, lcm_config_entry
) -> None:
    """Neither the PIN nor the password left: the edit is refused."""
    await _set_slot1_password(hass, lcm_config_entry, "pw")
    result = await _edit_user_form(hass, lcm_config_entry, 1)

    result = await _subentry_configure(
        hass, result["flow_id"], {CONF_NAME: "slot1", CONF_ENABLED: True}
    )

    assert result["errors"] == {"base": "missing_credential_if_enabled"}
    assert get_entry_config(lcm_config_entry).slot(1)["password"] == "pw"


def _refuse_passwords(real):
    async def _set(self, code_slot, credential_type, value, **kwargs):
        if credential_type is CredentialType.PASSWORD:
            raise CodeRejectedError(code_slot, self.lock.entity_id, "too simple")
        return await real(self, code_slot, credential_type, value, **kwargs)

    return _set


def _disabled_issue(hass: HomeAssistant, entry, slot: int = 1) -> ir.IssueEntry | None:
    return ir.async_get(hass).async_get_issue(
        DOMAIN, f"slot_disabled_{entry.entry_id}_{slot}"
    )


async def test_a_refused_password_turns_the_user_off_beside_a_working_pin(
    hass: HomeAssistant, lcm_config_entry
) -> None:
    """Any refused value turns the user off, whatever its type (decision 11)."""
    coordinator = lcm_config_entry.runtime_data.slot_coordinators[1]
    worker = lock_registry(hass).worker(VIRTUAL_LOCK_ENTITY_ID)
    assert worker is not None
    await _settled(hass)
    assert worker.status(pin_address(1)) == (Status.IN_SYNC, None)
    with patch.object(
        VirtualLock,
        "async_set_slot_credential",
        _refuse_passwords(VirtualLock.async_set_slot_credential),
    ):
        await coordinator.async_request_credential_update(CredentialType.PASSWORD, "pw")
        await _settled(hass)

    assert coordinator.is_enabled is False
    issue = _disabled_issue(hass, lcm_config_entry)
    assert issue is not None
    assert issue.translation_placeholders is not None
    assert "refused the password for slot" in issue.translation_placeholders["reason"]
    assert "too simple" in issue.translation_placeholders["reason"]


async def test_a_refused_only_credential_turns_the_slot_off(
    hass: HomeAssistant, lcm_config_entry
) -> None:
    """A password-only user whose password is refused is turned off."""
    coordinator = lcm_config_entry.runtime_data.slot_coordinators[1]
    await coordinator.async_request_credential_update(CredentialType.PIN, "")
    assert coordinator.is_enabled is False
    with patch.object(
        VirtualLock,
        "async_set_slot_credential",
        _refuse_passwords(VirtualLock.async_set_slot_credential),
    ):
        await coordinator.async_request_credential_update(CredentialType.PASSWORD, "pw")
        await coordinator.async_request_active_toggle(True)
        assert coordinator.is_enabled is True
        await _settled(hass)

    assert coordinator.is_enabled is False
    issue = _disabled_issue(hass, lcm_config_entry)
    assert issue is not None
    assert issue.translation_placeholders is not None
    assert "refused the password for slot" in issue.translation_placeholders["reason"]


async def test_a_new_user_with_a_refused_password_is_turned_off(
    hass: HomeAssistant, lcm_config_entry
) -> None:
    """
    A new user's PIN and refused password: off, as an existing user would be.

    The worker writes a new slot's password before its PIN, so the refusal
    arrives before the PIN is on the lock.

    with patch.object(

Author: raman325 <7243222+raman325@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Sun Oct 25 18:52:23 2026 -0400

    fix(config_flow): take a password the edit form doesn't show as stored
    
    When the entry's locks don't take passwords, editing a user carries their
    stored password into the submission. It then went through the value rule
    and the duplicate check, so a stored password the rule refuses (only
    hand-edited storage holds one) put an error on a field the form doesn't
    draw, and the dialog could never be submitted. A carried password is the
    user's stored value, not a submission: it skips both checks and still
    counts as the credential an enabled user needs.

    fix(config_flow): take a password the edit form doesn't show as stored
    
    When the entry's locks don't take passwords, editing a user carries their
    stored password into the submission. It then went through the value rule
    and the duplicate check, so a stored password the rule refuses (only
    hand-edited storage holds one) put an error on a field the form doesn't
    draw, and the dialog could never be submitted. A carried password is the
    user's stored value, not a submission: it skips both checks and still
    counts as the credential an enabled user needs.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

I'm realizing the test expectation would shift depending on which offered types are used, so it's more consistent to rely on the latched password-offered answer for the form that was actually drawn, since that defines what was genuinely offered.

Since `_password_offered` is a bool, I keep it as `bool | None` and derive offered types from it: PIN+PASSWORD if True, just PIN if False. For the None case — meaning a submit happened without a prior draw — that's essentially unreachable in practice since all flow entry points draw the form first, so I can safely compute it fresh there without breaking the patched test behavior.

I'm also considering a future-proofing concern: the form only ever displays PIN and password, so other credential types don't need to factor into "offered" logic. To avoid disrupting existing tests that patch `_offers_password`, I'll keep that method intact and just add a small helper that converts the latched bool into the actual offered-types frozenset.

This latched-at-draw-time behavior matches the stated rule: offered types are the loaded entry's available types, or PIN-only otherwise. Now I'm tracing through the carried-password test case to confirm it still keeps the stored password when the form didn't offer one.

So the previously accepted parameter case where the only credential a user has gets kept would now be refused instead — I should update that test to expect refusal, splitting it from the separate "password refused by rule" case, and adjust the docstring accordingly. I also need to check the code-slot flow: since its schema has no password field and extras are prevented by the schema validation, only PIN can ever be offered there, which is consistent.

For the YAML validation path, I'm adding a check after parsing that flags any enabled user lacking a valid credential for the offered types. The existing tests use the error key `invalid_config` for this path, so I should keep that key as-is rather than introducing `missing_credential_if_enabled`, since changing an existing test's expected value isn't allowed without flagging it.

I'll keep logging an error for parity with existing behavior, matching the message format used elsewhere, and place the credential check right after the schema parse to preserve the original ordering. The YAML path without loaded locks should still fall back to PIN-only validation.

Now I'm updating has_credential to require the offered collection as a parameter, updating all callers to pass it explicitly, then moving on to review the slot_coordinator code.

    ATTR_IN_SYNC,
    CREDENTIAL_LABELS,
    DOMAIN,
    EVENT_CREDENTIAL_USED,
    credential_noun,
)
from ..model.config import (

    async_write_entry_config,
    credential_holder,
    credential_values,
    has_credential,
)
from ..model.credentials import (
    MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_ORDER,
    CredentialType,
    credential_value_error,
)
from ..model.names import name_error, normalize_name
from ..model.queries import get_entry_config
from .runtime import async_want

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .entry import LockCodeManagerConfigEntry


_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)

        self._write_config_fields({CONF_NAME: name})

    async def async_request_credential_update(
        self, credential_type: CredentialType, value: str
    ) -> None:
        """
        Apply a credential write requested by a text entity or an action.

        A PIN is stripped: a submitted code is stripped before it is matched,
        so padding kept on the stored side makes a credential nothing typed
        can match. A password is kept as typed (spec decision 7).

        A non-empty value must pass the type's character rule and every bound
        lock's length range; an empty one clears the credential and is
        exempt. This is the authoritative gate: the text entity keeps
        ``native_min`` and ``native_max`` permissive so Home Assistant's
        ``text.set_value`` neither rejects the empty clear nor pre-empts the
        per-lock error built here -- whose errors would quote the value.

        Clearing the slot's last credential turns an enabled slot off: a user
        with nothing to present would read as active (spec decision 4).
        Clearing a credential the user does not hold writes nothing.
        """
        if credential_type is CredentialType.PIN:
            value = value.strip()
        if value:
            if error := credential_value_error(credential_type, value):
                raise ServiceValidationError(error)
            self._validate_credential_length(value, credential_type)
        held = credential_values(self._slot_config())
        if value and value != held.get(credential_type):
            self._refuse_duplicate(credential_type, value)

        updates: dict[str, Any] = {credential_type.value: value}
        if (
            not value
            and not any(other is not credential_type for other in held)
            and self.is_enabled
        ):
            _LOGGER.debug(
                "%s: last credential cleared on enabled slot, auto-disabling",
                self._log_prefix,
            )
            updates[CONF_ENABLED] = False
        elif not value and credential_type not in held:
            # Nothing to clear, and nothing else changes: no write, no pass.
            return

        self._write_config_fields(updates)

    def _refuse_duplicate(self, credential_type: CredentialType, value: str) -> None:
        """
        Refuse ``value`` if another user in the entry holds it as the same type.

        Two users sharing a credential: whoever presents it is recorded as
        either, and turning one off leaves it working (spec decision 12).
        Every user counts, one with no slot number too. Names the other user,
        never the value.
        """
        config = get_entry_config(self._config_entry)
        own = config.name_for(self._slot_num)
        others = {name: user for name, user in config.users.items() if name != own}
        if (other := credential_holder(others, credential_type, value)) is not None:
            noun = credential_noun(credential_type.value)
            raise ServiceValidationError(f"{other} already has this {noun}")

    def _validate_credential_length(
        self, value: str, credential_type: CredentialType
    ) -> None:
        """
        Reject ``value`` if it violates any bound lock's length range.

        Authoritative gate for credential length. Iterates every bound lock so
        the error names each offending lock with its required range. The lock
        set is the entry-wide ``runtime_data.locks`` -- the same set the text
        entity mirrors in ``self.locks`` to size its surfaced bounds, since LCM
        binds every lock to every slot; a future per-slot binding must update
        both sites together. Locks whose capabilities are not cached
        (disconnected or not yet probed) and locks that do not advertise
        ``credential_type`` are skipped -- the write proceeds rather than
        blocking on unknown limits, and the sync layer surfaces any later
        device rejection.
        """
        length = len(value)
        violations: list[str] = []
        for lock in self._config_entry.runtime_data.locks.values():
            caps = lock.cached_capabilities
            if caps is None:
                continue
            bounds = caps.length_bounds(credential_type)
            if bounds is None:
                continue
            lo, hi = bounds
            if length < lo or (hi is not None and length > hi):
                required = (
                    f"at least {lo} characters"
                    if hi is None
                    else f"{lo}-{hi} characters"
                )
                violations.append(f"{required} for {lock.display_name}")
        if violations:
            raise ServiceValidationError(
                f"{CREDENTIAL_LABELS[credential_type.value]} length {length} is not accepted "
                f"by all locks: {'; '.join(violations)}"
            )

    async def async_request_active_toggle(self, enabled: bool) -> None:
        """
        Apply an enabled/disabled toggle requested by the switch entity.

        Disable is unconditional. Enable needs a credential of any type and
        raises ``CredentialRequiredError`` without one (the switch translates
        that into ``HomeAssistantError``). The repairs an enable answers are
        deleted by ``_recompute_active``, which sees every route back on.
        """
        if not enabled:
            self._write_config_fields({CONF_ENABLED: False})
            return

        if not has_credential(self._slot_config()):
            self._safely_raise_credential_required_issue()
            raise CredentialRequiredError(
                f"Set a PIN or password for slot {self._slot_num} before enabling it"
            )

        self._write_config_fields({CONF_ENABLED: True})

    @callback
    def notify_config_changed(self) -> None:
        """
        React to a config entry change.

        Called by ``async_update_listener`` after it refreshes
        ``runtime_data.config``. Updates the condition-entity subscription
        if the condition entity moved, recomputes derived state, and
        fans the new state out to writers and to the entry's locks.

async def async_add_users(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    users: list[dict[str, Any]],
    *,
    config_entry_id: str | None = None,
    config_entry_title: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """
    Add one or more users to an entry, numbering them by reading the locks.

    All or nothing. Every name is validated, one allocation covers the whole
    batch, and one write lands it. Partial success would leave the caller
    working out which of a list arrived, and nothing here needs it: every way
    this can fail -- a name that means somebody already here, a batch that
    will not fit -- is knowable before anything is written.

    Adding N users one call at a time would read the locks N times, which on a
    battery lock is the difference between usable and not, and would settle
    the entry N times over.
    """
    config_entry = get_loaded_config_entry(hass, config_entry_id, config_entry_title)
    config = get_entry_config(config_entry)

    additions: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for entry in users:
        name = entry[CONF_NAME]
        if error := name_error(name):
            raise ServiceValidationError(f"Invalid name {name!r}: {error}")
        name = normalize_name(name)
        # Checked against the batch as well as the entry: two names in one
        # call meaning one person would collapse into a single key on the way
        # into storage, taking one of their credentials with it.
        if any(
            identity(known) == identity(name) for known in (*config.users, *additions)
        ):
            raise ServiceValidationError(f"A user named {name!r} already exists")

        credentials = credential_values(entry)
        enabled = entry.get(CONF_ENABLED, True)
        condition = entry.get(CONF_CONDITION)

        # The same rule the editor enforces: a slot cannot be programmed
        # without something to program.
        if enabled and not credentials:
            raise ServiceValidationError(
                f"{name!r} cannot be enabled without a PIN or password"
            )
        for credential_type, value in credentials.items():
            if error := credential_value_error(credential_type, value):
                raise ServiceValidationError(f"{name!r}: {error}")
            if (
                holder := credential_holder(
                    {**config.users, **additions}, credential_type, value
                )
            ) is not None:
                noun = credential_noun(credential_type.value)
                raise ServiceValidationError(
                    f"{name!r} cannot have the {noun} {holder!r} already has"
                )
        if condition:
            _async_validate_condition(hass, condition)

        user: dict[str, Any] = {
            CONF_ENABLED: enabled,
            **{
                credential_type.value: value
                for credential_type, value in credentials.items()
            },
        }
        if condition:
            user[CONF_CONDITION] = condition
        additions[name] = user

    try:
        # One read of the locks for the whole batch, sized to what the entry
        # will hold once it lands.
        unavailable = await async_allocate_for(
            hass,
            config_entry,
            config.locks,
            len(config.users) + len(additions),
            # Everyone already here stays, so their numbers need no read.
            held=config.assignment.held_by(config.users),
        )
    except SlotAllocationError as err:
        raise ServiceValidationError(
            translation_domain=DOMAIN,
            translation_key=err.translation_key,
            translation_placeholders={
                key: str(value) for key, value in err.placeholders.items()
            },
        ) from err

    # Reconciled against the whole set rather than issued directly: everyone
    # already here keeps their number by tenure, and only the newcomers are
    # given one.
    assignment = config.assignment.reconcile(
        [*config.users, *additions], start=1, unavailable=unavailable
    )
    await _async_write_and_settle(
        hass,
        config_entry,
        EntryConfig(
            locks=config.locks,
            users={**config.users, **additions},
            assignment=assignment,
            extra=config.extra,
        ),
    )

def _pin_caps(min_length: int, max_length: int) -> LockCapabilities:
    """Build LockCapabilities advertising a PIN type with the given bounds."""
    return LockCapabilities(
        supports_user_management=True,
        max_users=30,
        credential_types={
            CredentialType.PIN: CredentialTypeCapability(
                num_slots=30,
                min_length=min_length,
                max_length=max_length,
                supports_learn=False,

async def test_request_pin_update_auto_disables_on_empty(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    mock_lock_config_entry,
    lock_code_manager_config_entry,
):
    """Clearing the PIN on an enabled slot disables the slot in one write."""
    runtime_data = lock_code_manager_config_entry.runtime_data
    coordinator = runtime_data.slot_coordinators[1]
    assert coordinator.is_enabled is True
    assert coordinator.pin_value == "1234"

    await coordinator.async_request_credential_update(CredentialType.PIN, "")
    await hass.async_block_till_done()

    config = get_entry_config(lock_code_manager_config_entry).slot(1)
    assert config.get(CONF_PIN) == ""
    assert config.get(CONF_ENABLED) is False
    assert coordinator.is_enabled is False

    state = hass.states.get(SLOT_1_PIN_ENTITY)
    assert state is not None
    assert state.state == ""
    state = hass.states.get(SLOT_1_ENABLED_ENTITY)
    assert state is not None
    assert state.state == STATE_OFF


async def test_request_pin_update_normalizes_whitespace(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    mock_lock_config_entry,
    lock_code_manager_config_entry,
):
    """A whitespace-only PIN normalizes to empty and auto-disables the slot."""
    coordinator = lock_code_manager_config_entry.runtime_data.slot_coordinators[1]
    await coordinator.async_request_credential_update(CredentialType.PIN, "   ")
    await hass.async_block_till_done()

    config = get_entry_config(lock_code_manager_config_entry).slot(1)
    assert config.get(CONF_PIN) == ""
    assert config.get(CONF_ENABLED) is False


async def test_request_pin_update_strips_surrounding_whitespace(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    mock_lock_config_entry,
    lock_code_manager_config_entry,
):
    """
    A padded PIN is stored stripped, and its length is judged stripped too.

    Every consumer compares against the stored value stripped -- the
    validate_code action most visibly -- so storing the padding makes a
    PIN nobody can enter.
    """
    runtime_data = lock_code_manager_config_entry.runtime_data
    for lock in runtime_data.locks.values():
        lock._capabilities_cache = _pin_caps(4, 8)
    coordinator = runtime_data.slot_coordinators[1]

    await coordinator.async_request_credential_update(
        CredentialType.PIN, "  12345678  "
    )
    await hass.async_block_till_done()

    config = get_entry_config(lock_code_manager_config_entry).slot(1)
    assert config.get(CONF_PIN) == "12345678"
    assert config.get(CONF_ENABLED) is True


async def test_request_active_toggle_blocks_when_no_pin(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    mock_lock_config_entry,
    lock_code_manager_config_entry,
):
    """Toggling active=True without a PIN raises and writes a repair issue."""
    coordinator = lock_code_manager_config_entry.runtime_data.slot_coordinators[1]
    # Clear PIN first (auto-disables the slot)
    await coordinator.async_request_credential_update(CredentialType.PIN, "")
    await hass.async_block_till_done()
    assert coordinator.is_enabled is False
    assert coordinator.pin_value is None

    with pytest.raises(CredentialRequiredError):
        await coordinator.async_request_active_toggle(True)

    issue_registry = async_get_issue_registry(hass)
    issue = issue_registry.async_get_issue(
        DOMAIN, f"credential_required_{lock_code_manager_config_entry.entry_id}_1"
    )
    assert issue is not None
    assert coordinator.is_enabled is False


async def test_request_active_toggle_clears_credential_required_issue(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    mock_lock_config_entry,
    lock_code_manager_config_entry,
):
    """Successful enable removes the credential_required repair issue."""
    coordinator = lock_code_manager_config_entry.runtime_data.slot_coordinators[1]
    await coordinator.async_request_credential_update(CredentialType.PIN, "")
    await hass.async_block_till_done()
    with pytest.raises(CredentialRequiredError):
        await coordinator.async_request_active_toggle(True)
    issue_registry = async_get_issue_registry(hass)
    assert (
        issue_registry.async_get_issue(
            DOMAIN, f"credential_required_{lock_code_manager_config_entry.entry_id}_1"
        )
        is not None
    )

    # Re-add a PIN and successfully enable; the repair issue must be cleared
    await coordinator.async_request_credential_update(CredentialType.PIN, "4242")
    await hass.async_block_till_done()
    await coordinator.async_request_active_toggle(True)
    await hass.async_block_till_done()

    assert coordinator.is_enabled is True
    assert (
        issue_registry.async_get_issue(
            DOMAIN, f"credential_required_{lock_code_manager_config_entry.entry_id}_1"
        )
        is None
    )

async def test_add_user_service_stores_a_padded_pin_stripped(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    mock_lock_config_entry,
    lock_code_manager_config_entry,
) -> None:
    """
    A PIN handed to the service with padding is stored without it.

    The service writes the entry's users directly, the way both flows do,
    so it is the third door onto the same storage -- and a submitted code
    is stripped before it is matched.
    """
    entry = lock_code_manager_config_entry
    await hass.services.async_call(
        DOMAIN,
        SERVICE_ADD_USER,
        {
            "config_entry_id": entry.entry_id,
            CONF_NAME: "Newcomer",
            CONF_PIN: " 9876 ",
        },
        blocking=True,
    )
    await hass.async_block_till_done()

    config = get_entry_config(hass.config_entries.async_get_entry(entry.entry_id))
    assert config.users["Newcomer"][CONF_PIN] == "9876"

async def _start_user_subentry_flow(
    hass: HomeAssistant, entry: MockConfigEntry, *, path: str = "one"
) -> str:
    """Open the flow that adds users to an entry, and return its flow id.

    Adding opens on a choice of one user or a block of them, so a test that
    wants a form says which it came for.
    """
    result = await hass.config_entries.subentries.async_init(
        (entry.entry_id, SUBENTRY_TYPE_USER), context={"source": SOURCE_USER}
    )
    assert result["type"] == "menu"
    assert result["step_id"] == "user"

    result = await hass.config_entries.subentries.async_configure(
        result["flow_id"], {"next_step_id": path}
    )
    assert result["type"] == "form"
    assert result["step_id"] == path
    return result["flow_id"]

## Proposed change

The third of five PRs toward password credentials. A user can now hold a password as well as, or instead of, a PIN. It is stored in their configuration, and Lock Code Manager keeps it in sync on every lock in the entry that takes passwords. Only Virtual locks take passwords until the Z-Wave PR.

- **Where a password is set:**
  - A **Password** text entity per user, present while a lock in the entry takes passwords. At the end of each update the entities are matched to the entry's locks in one step, so locks joining and leaving in any combination add or remove them; the stored password stays.
  - The **`set_credential`** and **`clear_credential`** actions take `credential_type: password`. **`add_user`** takes `password`.
  - The **add-user and edit-user dialogs** show a Password field, next to PIN, when the entry's locks take passwords. Editing a user keeps a stored password the dialog doesn't show. Pasted users (YAML) take `password:`.
- **What a password may be:** printable characters and spaces, kept exactly as typed (a PIN is still stripped). Any credential, PIN included, may be at most 255 characters, Home Assistant's limit for a text entity's state. A password of only spaces is refused, as a blank PIN is. Each lock's own length range applies when a credential is set from the entity or `set_credential` (the dialogs and `add_user` don't check it, for PINs as before). Errors name the rule, never the value.
- **A user needs a PIN or a password to be enabled.** Clearing one credential turns the user off only when it was their last. The `pin_required` repair is now `credential_required`; a leftover `pin_required` repair is deleted at setup and can still be acknowledged.
- **Duplicates are refused when a credential is set,** for PINs as well as passwords: a value another user in the entry already holds as the same type is refused, including a user who is turned off. A password may equal a PIN. A value a user already held (a duplicate saved before this rule) isn't refused until it changes. The lock's own duplicate check stays as the backstop.
- **When a lock refuses a credential, the user is turned off,** whatever the credential's type, as a refused PIN does today. The `slot_disabled` repair names the refused credential. It is answered when the user is turned back on, by any route (switch, action, dialog), or once every credential the user wants is on the lock. A `credential_required` repair is answered the same way on any re-enable.
- **Logs and diagnostics:** a password is masked as a `pwd#…` token, apart from a PIN with the same value. `deobfuscate_log` decodes both, and slot diagnostics show the masked password. A PIN's tokens are unchanged.

**Behavior changes on every install, PIN-only locks included:**
- Setting a PIN another user in the entry holds is refused, from the entity, the actions, the dialogs and pasted YAML. Before, the lock refused it and the user was turned off.
- An enabled user with neither a PIN nor a password is refused with "A PIN or password must be set". The dialog's error moves from the PIN field to the form.
- Re-enabling a user from the edit dialog now answers their `slot_disabled` and `credential_required` repairs, as the switch does.
- `set_credential` no longer strips its `value` in the schema; a PIN is still stripped, and a blank PIN is refused.
- A PIN over 255 characters is refused.

**Known limit:** a value over 255 characters sent straight to `text.set_value` is refused by Home Assistant itself, before Lock Code Manager sees it, with an error that quotes the value.

**Testing:**
- New tests cover each path on a Virtual lock: the entity, the actions, the dialogs and pasted users; the credential-required rule; duplicates per type, including turned-off users and unchanged values; a refused password turning the user off for a new and an existing user alike; repairs answered on re-enable from every route and on sync; the password entity's lifecycle as locks join and leave, including two password locks removed in one update and a swap; masking and deobfuscation. A leak test submits a marked value and checks it appears in neither the error nor the logs.
- **Mutation checks:** each rule was broken on purpose, and a named test failed every time.
- **Full suite:** passes, apart from the three paced tests that flake when run in parallel (each passes on its own). Coverage equals `main` (53 missed lines, 99%), with no file gaining an uncovered line. Property tests pass at the CI profile.
- One Matter test now judges the deletion by state transitions: an attribute rewrite landing late was failing it under load.

content.text:
**Status: DONE_WITH_CONCERNS.** The rule is in, every requested test and mutation behaves as asked, and the full suite and `prek` pass. There is one commit, **24483fac**, on top of 3d83bbf7. Nothing was amended or pushed. Two items below don't match your brief, and you should look at them before this goes up.

## Concerns

1. **The pasted-YAML error key.** Your brief says to refuse with `missing_credential_if_enabled`, "the YAML path's error key as it is today". But today both YAML paths (setup and `several`) return `invalid_config` for this, because the check sat inside `USERS_SCHEMA`. Two existing PIN-only tests expect `invalid_config`: `test_config_flow_yaml_error` and `test_config_flow_yaml_rejects_a_whitespace_only_pin`. I kept `invalid_config`, so those tests are unchanged, and my new YAML tests assert it. Switching to `missing_credential_if_enabled` is a one-line change, but it changes what PIN-only users see.
2. **Which types the dialogs accept.** The add and edit dialogs use the types the form showed when it was first drawn, using the existing `_password_offered` setting. They only look at the entry again when no form was drawn. A fresh look at submit time would break `test_the_add_dialog_keeps_the_password_field_it_first_drew`, which fakes "passwords offered" on a PIN-only entry and expects a password-only user to save.

Two smaller points:
- **Error messages still say "PIN or password",** even on PIN-only entries, where that's misleading. Naming only the types the entry takes would change the expected message in `test_switch_entity` and `test_switch_turn_on_raises_homeassistanterror_for_credential_required`, so I backed it out. It's a candidate follow-up.
- **One small behaviour change in clearing.** The clear check keeps its old structure with the new rule. So clearing any credential while a user is enabled without a counting credential now turns them off. That's a leftover state, for example an enabled password-only user whose password lock left the entry. Before, clearing a PIN they didn't hold wrote nothing.

## What changed
- **`model/config.py`:** `has_credential(user, offered)` now needs the entry's offered types. The old one-argument form had no callers left, so it's gone.
- **Switch enable and clearing (`ha/slot_coordinator.py`):** enabling refuses with `CredentialRequiredError` unless the user has a credential of a type in `available_credential_types(entry)`. A clear turns an enabled user off when nothing of an offered type remains.
- **`add_user` (`ha/services.py`):** an enabled user needs a credential of an offered type.
- **Config flow (`config_flow.py`):**
  - The setup form and setup YAML offer PIN only.
  - The `several` step uses the entry's types if it's loaded, PIN only otherwise.
  - The "enabled needs a credential" check moved out of `USERS_SCHEMA` into `_async_validate_users_yaml`.
- A stored password is never deleted anywhere.

## Existing test whose expected value changed
`test_editing_a_user_takes_a_password_the_form_does_not_offer_as_stored` from 1f5cc403. It covered two cases:
- **Kept as it was:** a PIN user whose stored password breaks the character rule can still be edited.
- **Moved to a new test:** the password-only user. `test_a_password_the_form_does_not_offer_does_not_enable_a_user` now expects `missing_credential_if_enabled`, with the password still stored. A password the edit form carries because no lock takes passwords no longer counts.

## New tests
All on the PIN-only mock entry:
- **(a)** `test_slot_coordinator.py::test_clearing_the_pin_beside_a_password_no_lock_takes_turns_the_user_off`
- **(b)** `test_slot_coordinator.py::test_a_password_no_lock_takes_cannot_enable_a_user`
- **(c)** `test_services.py::test_add_user_service_rejects_enabled_with_a_password_no_lock_takes`
- **(d)** `test_config_flow.py::TestUserFormsOnALoadedEntry::test_a_pasted_user_with_only_a_password_no_lock_takes_is_refused`, using the `several` path.
- **Setup flow:** `test_config_flow.py::test_config_flow_yaml_refuses_an_enabled_user_with_only_a_password`

The Virtual-entry password-only tests pass unchanged.

## Mutation checks
I used `/tmp/lcm-mut/mutate.py`, which restores each file in `finally`. `git diff` was clean after every run.

| Mutation | Test that failed |
|---|---|
| Enable check counts every stored type | (b) |
| Clear check counts every stored type | (a), and (b) |
| `add_user` counts every stored type | (c) |
| YAML check counts every stored type (extra) | the setup-flow test and (d) |
| Form check counts every stored type (extra) | the new password-not-offered edit test |
| YAML or form forced to PIN only (extra) | existing Virtual tests, e.g. `test_pasted_users_may_carry_a_password` and `test_a_user_with_only_a_password_can_be_added_enabled` |

## Test runs
- **Affected files** (`test_config_flow`, `test_password_config`, `test_services`, `test_slot_coordinator`, `test_switch`, `test_text`): all pass.
- **Full suite with `-n auto`:** 3567 passed, 3 failed. The failures were the three paced tests you named, and they pass when run on their own (4 passed).
- **`prek run --all-files`:** all hooks pass, mypy included.

## PR body
The credential bullet in `/tmp/lcm-pr2b/pr-body.md` now says:
- a credential counts only if a lock in the entry takes its type;
- a stored password is kept but doesn't count while no lock takes passwords;
- the setup flow offers PIN only.

I didn't touch the "Behavior changes" section.

**Files changed:** `custom_components/lock_code_manager/{model/config.py, ha/slot_coordinator.py, ha/services.py, config_flow.py}` and `tests/{test_config_flow.py, test_services.py, test_slot_coordinator.py}`, all under `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/.worktrees/password-config/`.
